This shows the most recent command in your shell history. To copy it, you have a few options:

   ```bash
   last_cmd=$(history | tail -1 | sed 's/^[ ]*[0-9]*[ ]*//')
   ```

   ```bash
   history | tail -1 | sed 's/^[ ]*[0-9]*[ ]*//' | xclip -selection clipboard
   ```

3. **Pipe to clipboard** (macOS):

   ```bash
   history | tail -1 | sed 's/^[ ]*[0-9]*[ ]*//' | pbcopy
   ```
